Save button writes sliders to config file

## Goal

AC3 of parent AH-0MT9FS3DL0084Z6V: a Save button persists the current slider values to the config file via the config module, with success/failure feedback.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Save button:** The gym UI panel renders a Save button.
- [ ] **AC2 — Persists values:** Clicking Save calls saveShipConfig(currentValues) where currentValues are the panel slider/color values; values survive reload (loadShipConfig returns them).
- [ ] **AC3 — Feedback:** A status message (e.g. "Saved") appears on success; error shows failure text.
- [ ] **AC4 — Tests:** happy-dom test clicks Save, asserts saveShipConfig persisted to localStorage key ai-hell-ship-config and a status message rendered.

## Key Files

- src/scenes/Gym.ts
- src/core/config.ts (saveShipConfig)

# Per-engine flame rendering with component scaling

## Goal
Replace the single centre-anchored flame with per-engine flames: draw a flame from each engine port whose outward normal opposes the current thrust vector, each flame scaled by the thrust component along that axis.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **AC1 — Cardinal thrust fires one engine:**
  - Thrust right → left engine fires
  - Thrust left → right engine fires
  - Thrust up → bottom engine fires
  - Thrust down → top engine fires
  (The engine whose outward normal OPPOSES the thrust direction.)
- **AC2 — Diagonal thrust fires two engines:**
  - Up+right → bottom engine (scale 1.0) and left engine (scale 1.0)
  - All four diagonal combinations covered
  - Each flame's length is scaled by its thrust component (e.g., thrust up=0.5, right=1.0 → bottom flame at 0.5× length, left flame at 1.0× length)
- **AC3 — No thrust → no flames:** When no direction keys are held, no flames are drawn from any port.
- **AC4 — Flame animation reuses flame.ts:** Each engine's flame uses the same dt-based growth/shrink animation from `utils/flame.ts` (`updateFlameLength`). Each engine tracks its own flame length.
- **AC5 — Flame length scaled by component:** A flame from engine E scales its animated length by the thrust component magnitude (e.g., thrust right=1.0 → full flame; thrust right=0.5 → 0.5× flame length). The max flame length is still `shipSize × thrustFlameLength`.

## Implementation notes
- Each engine port tracks its own `_flameLen` (or compute per-engine flame lengths in `_drawFlame()`).
- The flame direction from each port goes OUTWARD from the port (away from hull centre), i.e., along the port's outward normal.
- Flame geometry per port is identical to the current flame geometry (outer triangle + inner triangle), just repositioned to the port location and rotated to match the outward normal.
- The current `_drawFlame()` logic computes a single flame from a normalised direction; refactor to accept a per-engine direction, length, and position.
- Reuse the flame animation from `AH-0MTAF5YLT009TXAM` (flame.ts `updateFlameLength`) — the flame item is already merged and provides the dt-based growth/shrink semantics.

## Key Files
- `src/entities/Player.ts` — refactor `_redraw()` to draw per-engine flames; add per-engine flame length state; refactor `_drawFlame()` or replace with per-engine flame drawing
- `src/utils/engineSelection.ts` — used by this item for determining which engines fire

## Dependencies
- `AH-0MTBOIIF6004GPY8` — Direction-neutral hexagon body shape (engine ports positioned on the hull)
- `AH-0MTBOE8JM0040Z3Y` — Pure helper: MovementInput → {firingEngines, flameScales}

## Deliverables
- Per-engine flame rendering replacing the single centre flame
- Per-engine flame animation using flame.ts
- Flame length scaled by thrust component

## Related AC
- Parent AC3 — Engine firing rule

# Player entity tests: body shape, engine ports, per-engine flames

## Goal
Update and extend Player tests to cover the new direction-neutral body, engine ports, and per-engine flame rendering. Since Phaser Graphics rendering is hard to assert pixel-level in happy-dom, use structural assertions (drawing command counts, geometry verification) and behavioural tests (flame length via exposed state).

## Acceptance Criteria
- **AC1 — Body shape structural test:** Verify `_redraw()` produces a hexagon (6 line segments) instead of the chevron (4 line segments). Use a spy on `Graphics.lineTo()` calls or inspect the drawing commands.
- **AC2 — Engine port drawing:** Verify the renderer draws 4 small arc commands (one per port) as part of the redraw. Structural test — count arc drawing calls.
- **AC3 — Cardinal thrust flame:** For each cardinal input (up, down, left, right), verify that exactly one engine flame appears at the correct port location. Use a spy on flame drawing calls or verify the flame length state for the correct engine.
- **AC4 — Diagonal thrust flame:** For diagonal inputs, verify two flames fire from the correct ports.
- **AC5 — No thrust → no flames:** Verify that with no input, no flame drawing commands are issued.
- **AC6 — Flame length scaling:** Verify that diagonal thrust with mixed components produces proportionally scaled flames (e.g., up=0.5, right=1.0 → bottom flame shorter than left flame).
- **AC7 — setConfig with new rendering:** Verify `setConfig` still live-tunes colours and re-draws the ship with the new shape and engine ports.

## Key Files
- `src/entities/Player.test.ts` — add/modify tests for body shape, engine ports, per-engine flames

## Dependencies
- `AH-0MTBOE8JM0040Z3Y` — Pure helper: MovementInput → {firingEngines, flameScales} (provides testable engine selection for flame tests)

## Deliverables
- Comprehensive Player entity tests covering all new rendering features
- Full project test suite passes

## Related AC
- Parent AC5 — Tests

data.description:
## Problem statement

The player ship's thrust flame keeps its current animated length when the pressed direction keys change (e.g. switching from Up to Left, or adding/removing a direction key mid-thrust). The flame simply re-orients to the new direction while keeping its length (see the 'flame's direction changed while a flame is visible' redraw branch in src/entities/Player.ts::preUpdate). The producer wants each change of the pressed keys to start a fresh flame burst from length 0.

## Desired change

When the set of pressed direction keys (up/down/left/right) changes while thrusting, the animated flame length must reset to 0 and regrow from there in the new direction, at the normal growth rate (proportional to thrustAcceleration).

- Pressed-key change (any direction-key state change) while a direction is held → flame length resets to 0 immediately on that frame.
- The flame then grows from 0 toward shipSize × thrustFlameLength at the existing rate (time-to-full = 0.03 s × (300 / thrustAcceleration) at reference thrust).
- Releasing all keys keeps existing decay semantics (decay at 4× growth rate; length never below 0) — no stuck flame.
- Unchanged held keys must NOT reset the flame (normal growth/decay continue).
- Existing feel tuning (FLAME_GROWTH_TIME_AT_REF = 0.03 s), framerate independence (delta-time based), and config-live max length are unchanged.

discovered-from:AH-0MTAF5YLT009TXAM

## Acceptance criteria

- AC1: Changing the pressed keys while thrusting resets the observable flame length (getFlameLength()) to 0 on that frame.
- AC2: The flame regrows from 0 in the new direction at the normal growth rate (higher thrustAcceleration → reaches full faster).
- AC3: Releasing all keys still decays the flame (4× growth rate) to 0 — no stuck flame on release.
- AC4: Holding the same keys does not reset the length — the flame continues growing/decaying normally frame to frame.
- AC5: Full test suite and tsc build remain green; docs (Player.ts header, GDD §2.2) updated to describe the reset-on-key-change behavior.
data.title: Reset thrust flame length to 0 when the pressed keys change
